$comment: Per-processor required document sets. THIS IS THE FILE THAT IS HAND-EDITED.
Adding a processor is one entry in `processors` and nothing else — no code, no schema change,
no migration. That property is the whole point of splitting this from documents.checks.json
(D-101), and there is a test that proves it rather than asserting it.
Every `slot_key` must name an entry in documents.checks.json's catalog. The loader refuses to
load if one does not — a requirement that silently does not exist is worse than a missing one,
and a warning on startup is a line nobody reads in a log nobody opens.
Coverage is expressed in the terms D-113 already settled; it is not redefined here. `monthly`
means the required months are the last complete calendar months ending on or before
(run date − grace), counted back `required_count` times. Slot states are D-107's six.
origin:  required     — always in the set
conditional  — in the set unless a predicate makes it structurally impossible (D-081)
added        — never seeded; an operator adds named instances (D-112)

predicate_inputs.$comment: The three questions asked at package creation. Nothing else may be predicated on.

processors.label: Default requirement set
processors.note: From CHECK-INVENTORY §4. The only set supplied so far; a per-processor set is an entry beside this one.

slots.note: Default-on for every package including startups (D-081). 'Startup' is not structural impossibility — plenty of new merchants have processing history under another entity — so the slot stays and resolves to not_provided with a reason. The report then says we asked and there are none.
required_count null means unknown, and unknown is not zero. Until the ownership section is read we do not know how many to expect, so the slot is not_evaluable rather than missing (D-107).
A sole proprietorship has no articles. Structural impossibility — D-081's first example.

Two slots with opposite predicates, not one row accepting either (D-111). One slot would be satisfied by whichever arrived, so a domestic entity filing a W-8BEN would satisfy its tax-form requirement with a document that cannot exist for it.
Off by default. D-102 item 3 leaves it open whether this becomes required; seeded as a definition so turning it on is a flag rather than a schema change.

No variable-count slots (D-112). An operator adds named instances, each with a count of 1 — 'state pharmacy licence' beside 'city business licence'. A 0..n slot could not tell 'no licence required' from 'no licence supplied'.
Requires an operator-supplied label at the point of adding (§3). Otherwise the report line reads 'Additional Document: satisfied', which tells the reader nothing.
